hints.title: Keep the exact area and its estimate separate
hints.body: Call the exact integral I and the trapezium estimate T. The information given is T<I. You need a transformation that reverses this inequality.
hints.recap: An underestimate means the numerical approximation is smaller than the exact integral.
hints.pitfall: An underestimate for one partition does not tell you the curve has the same curvature everywhere.
hints.pause: Consider what each transformation does to both T and I.

recall.reminder: An underestimate means the numerical approximation is smaller than the exact integral.

hints.title: Transform estimate and integral together
hints.body: Apply each offered transformation separately to both the estimate and the exact integral. The trapezium rule integrates a constant exactly, so any constant contribution can be found directly.
hints.recap: Track the change in the signed error as well as the change in the area.
hints.pitfall: A horizontal transformation needs a corresponding check of the integration bounds.
hints.pause: For each candidate write the transformed estimate and exact integral, then compare their order.

recall.reminder: Track the change in the signed error as well as the change in the area.

solution:
1. Name the estimate. Let I=∫01f(x)dx and let T be its trapezium estimate, so T<I.

2. Check the transformations that preserve underestimation. In A, the exact integral and estimate become I+1 and T+1. In B, they become 2I and 2T. C translates both the graph and its interval left by 1; D reflects them in the vertical axis. These horizontal changes preserve the exact area and the trapezium sum, so C and D also remain underestimates.

3. Use the complement. For E, every height becomes one minus its former height. The exact integral is 1−I. The trapezium rule is exact for the constant height 1, so its new estimate is 1−T. As T<I, we get 1−T>1−I: an overestimate.

Answer E. This compares the estimates directly and does not require guessing a curve shape.
knowledgePattern: Use linearity of trapezium-rule error under transformations
